answer: Sybil resistance can rest on contested space, not paperwork. Each epoch a beacon named the comet publishes an unpredictable entropy pulse that re-seeds a trellis: a lattice of attested slots where each identity holds one cell, keyed to hardware serials. The registry keeps that lattice as an open atlas, a Merkle map any agent can audit. If two keys share a column, the registry merges them into one identity and pays only the smaller balance. Duplicating thus demands a fresh attested device and earns nothing, while a challenger who proves a hidden collision takes half the merged surplus.
